rationale:
RESUBMISSION of the identical shipped change (commit 4b3f9f89b, live v1.0.1251, pod-verified `strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -c "single-unmatched-prose-slot"` = 1 on both replicas) after round 1 (correlation 56f9a5a2-4d37-4114-9442-239861acd36e) returned REVISE, gated by bug_historian at HIGH severity, with two further objections (architecture MEDIUM, prior_art_librarian MEDIUM) all circling the same underlying question: does this narrow fix leave a shared assumption unaddressed elsewhere. The other 8 reviewers approved (editquality, reuse_agent, guardian, diagnosis_guardian, compliance, render_guardian, debug_historian, constitution, mission), several noting the scoping (opt-in gate, read-only enrichment, no write-path change) as exactly right.

No code changed since round 1 — this submission answers the three objections with read-only checks, per this repo's own council-gate practice for a REVISE round.

OBJECTION 1 (bug_historian, HIGH, gating): 'a shared mechanism — does the current build's resolved component_name match the page's previously stored slot_name — is already broken on other paths (save_page_sections_action.go, rerender_page_sections_action.go), which are left exposed to the identical silent-fabrication failure.' CHECKED, and the claim does not hold for either named file:
  - rerender_page_sections_action.go (lines 234-276): does NOT do an exact slot_name==component_name join. Since bugs_open/182 it resolves page_components.component_id FIRST — the row's own stored identity, immune to naming drift — and only falls back to the name/function map when component_id is absent. When both routes resolve and disagree, it logs observe-only ('component_id and slot_name resolve to different components (observe-only, id wins)', measured 2026-08-03: 13 live sections fleet-wide) and the id wins. This is a DIFFERENT, already-hardened mechanism, not a sibling of the exact-name join load_current_section_content_action.go had before this fix.
  - save_page_sections_action.go: is not a stale-row lookup at all. It DELETEs the page's existing components and INSERTs a fresh row per section of the new composition (each carrying its own resolved component_id from that build), so there is no 'does the old slot_name match the new name' join to silently miss. The one slot_name-keyed lookup in this file is matchLockedRow, a narrow, already-disclosed exception (bugs_open/058, human-locked rows only) — not the general write path.
  Neither cited file shares the failure mode this fix patches. The mechanism this fix targets — an opt-in READ enrichment step joining a build's resolved section list to a page's stored rows by exact slot_name, with a silent miss on drift — is, on the evidence available, unique to load_current_section_content_action.go's pre-fallback code.

OBJECTION 2 (architecture, MEDIUM): same underlying concern — content_components' name resolution is not guaranteed stable build-to-build, and any FUTURE direct joiner will rediscover this. This is correct and not disputed: the instability itself (why a build's resolved name can differ from an earlier build's stored slot_name) is bugs_open/178's own fix candidate 3, deliberately left open. It was ACTIVELY investigated this session: 090 diagnosis run (correlation 167d2cc2-0b98-405c-a1d7-d54d80ed37c9) against the one witnessed occurrence (guide-independent-strategy, vetcomparison.uk) ran 5 iterations and returned UNVERIFIABLE (stopped: scope-not-narrowing) — it could not obtain a page_component_history row predating the overwrite event under investigation, so the actual prior-build write path could not be named from available evidence, not merely left unexamined. bugs_open/178 records this as still open, now with a completed-but-inconclusive diagnosis attached rather than an untried item. Recommend the follow-up architecture flagged (RFC-level look at stable per-position content identity) be tracked explicitly rather than left as prose in a bug file: bugs_open/178 is a live, indexed OPEN case (016b §10) precisely so a future consumer hitting this same drift is directed there rather than re-discovering it. No code change proposed here; the deferral was already disclosed in round 1 and remains disclosed, now with the diagnosis attempt's negative result added as evidence that the gap is not for want of looking.

OBJECTION 3 (prior_art_librarian, MEDIUM): asks whether a content-identity matching mechanism already exists (cites datahelpers.SectionIdentityKey, used by check_content_duplication.go and remove_duplicate_page_sections_action.go) that this fallback risks duplicating. CHECKED by reading SectionIdentityKey's own definition and doc comment (datahelpers/section_text.go:93-163): it is explicitly NOT a content-identity matcher across different slots. Its contract requires slot equality as a NECESSARY condition ('SLOT EQUALITY IS NECESSARY... Two different components in two different slots are not the same section rendered twice, whatever their content_data happens to contain') plus byte-identical canonical content_data — it answers 'is this the same section rendered twice in the same slot', for safe deletion of exact duplicates (bugs_open/156's council round 2). This fallback answers the opposite-shaped question — 'is this DIFFERENT slot's content plausibly the SAME section under a NEW name' — for read-only enrichment, not deletion, gated to require unambiguity (exactly one candidate on each side) precisely because, unlike SectionIdentityKey's byte-equality test, there is no deterministic identity check available here. No existing mechanism in the codebase solves this specific problem; the fallback is not a duplicate build of prior art, it addresses a distinct question SectionIdentityKey's own documentation explicitly declines to answer.

plan.summary: No code change from round 1 — load_current_section_content_action.go (bugs_open/178's edit_live channel, opt-in via spec.mode='edit_live', default OFF for every other caller) gains a second, narrower match: when exactly one ready section misses the exact slot_name join AND exactly one still-unclaimed page_components row on the page is prose-sized (>=500 stripped chars, reusing the shrink guard's own minShrinkGuardChars/shrinkGuardTagStripper), that row's rendered_html is attached to that section as existing_content_html. Two or more of either side is left unmatched — no guessing. Already live (commit 4b3f9f89b, v1.0.1251, pod-verified both replicas). This resubmission's only change is the rationale, answering round 1's three objections with read-only code/doc checks rather than assertion.

edits.rationale: Unchanged from round 1 (56f9a5a2). This is the one place a page's stored prose is joined to the current build's section plan for editing. The exact-match loop is untouched; the fallback is additive and only ever fires inside the already-opt-in edit_live gate, bounded to the two live emitters that set mode='edit_live'.
Unchanged from round 1. Three new cases, mutation-proven against a git-stash revert of the fallback code.
edits.sketch: See file — reuses the existing newInsertMock/sqlmock scaffolding already in this file; no new test infrastructure.

grounded_in: ROUND 1 VERDICT, READ IN FULL: council_report for correlation 56f9a5a2-4d37-4114-9442-239861acd36e (diagnosis_artifacts, kind=council_report) — decision revise, decided_by 'gating objection from bug_historian', 5 approvals with low-severity notes only, 3 objections (bug_historian HIGH, architecture MEDIUM, prior_art_librarian MEDIUM).

OBJECTION 1 CHECKED AGAINST CODE: rerender_page_sections_action.go:234-276 resolves page_components.component_id before slot_name (bugs_open/182 fix), logging observe-only on disagreement rather than silently missing. save_page_sections_action.go is delete+insert per build (lines ~660-780), not a stale-row join; its only slot_name-keyed lookup is matchLockedRow (bugs_open/058), a disclosed, narrow exception.

OBJECTION 2: 090 diagnosis run against the one witnessed occurrence (guide-independent-strategy, page_id 2a347990-c152-4fa2-8acb-a39a5f74f4a9) — correlation 167d2cc2-0b98-405c-a1d7-d54d80ed37c9, 5 iterations, result UNVERIFIABLE/'NOT CONFIRMED (stopped: scope-not-narrowing)'. No page_component_history row predates the 2026-08-04 09:04:48 overwrite event under investigation, so the prior write path could not be named from available evidence.

OBJECTION 3 CHECKED AGAINST CODE: datahelpers/section_text.go:93-163, SectionIdentityKey doc comment — 'SLOT EQUALITY IS NECESSARY... Two different components in two different slots are not the same section rendered twice, whatever their content_data happens to contain.' Requires byte-identical canonical content_data plus same slot_name; built for exact-duplicate deletion (bugs_open/156 round 2), not cross-slot content matching.

Everything from round 1 stands: the diffed failure (guide-independent-strategy, 3637 chars replaced by 3262 wholly different chars), the fleet measurement (3/127 pages, 2.4%, stated lower bound), the shrink-guard constant reuse, and the mutation evidence (git stash of the action file fails all three new tests against pre-fallback code).
plan.risks: Unchanged from round 1: scope is bounded to the opt-in edit_live gate (2 emitters); a wrong pairing in the unambiguous case is possible but bounded by downstream write-time guards and cannot delete or overwrite; root cause (why component-name resolution can drift) remains open as bugs_open/178 candidate 3, now with a completed-but-inconclusive diagnosis attached (167d2cc2) rather than untried. NEW: this resubmission's own claim that rerender_page_sections_action.go and save_page_sections_action.go do not share the exact-slot_name-join failure mode is a code-reading exercise, not a fleet-wide test — a reviewer should re-check the cited line ranges rather than take the claim on trust, same standard this submission is holding round 1's objections to.
